## Appendix G: Detailed model specification and evaluation {.unnumbered}

### Model purposes and evaluation design {.unnumbered}

| Model or comparison | Purpose | Information used |
|---|---|---|
| Annual full-extent habitat model, 13 predictors | Predict cull outcomes across the full habitat-map extent | Twelve terrain and coral-habitat predictors plus survey year; fitted to cull site-years |
| Annual limited-extent habitat model, 18 predictors | Test whether added environmental information improves the annual prediction | The same predictors and year, plus five ReefGuide layers; fitted to cull site-years |
| Manta habitat models | Rank tow locations with strong COTS evidence | The environmental predictors above, fitted to tow observations; versions with year and with differences among reef-years accounted for were compared |
| Recent-evidence site ranking | Set a search order for designated cull sites | Habitat rank plus the preceding season's cull dives and nearby manta tows |
| Multi-observation habitat model | Explain habitat associations while allowing for different observations | Cull, SALAD and RHIS evidence, terrain, geomorphic classes and coral habitat; implemented with a hierarchical model of species communities |
| Habitat updated by longer cull history | Test how much past finds add to a habitat forecast | Multi-observation habitat estimates and spatially weighted earlier cull records |
| COTS–coral metacommunity model | Simulate connected populations, coral consumption and responses to removals | Population and coral processes, larval supply, disturbance and historical culling in the Lizard Island cluster |

: Models and comparisons. Predictor counts for the two annual models include survey year. Original code labels and alternative combinations are mapped to these descriptions in Appendix G. {#tbl-model-purpose}

| Decision | How the prediction was tested | Comparison and outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Where habitat predicts COTS | Each reef was scored by models fitted without its group of reefs | Ability to rank observations on the same reef and in the same year |
| Which cull sites to search | All designated sites were ranked, including never-dived sites; recent evidence came only from earlier seasons | Habitat alone, recent evidence and their combination; sites searched and dive outcomes retained |
| Whether the ranking works in later seasons | The evidence model was fitted on seasons before each test season, 2019–2026 | The same search outcomes, evaluated season by season |
| Whether >0.04 dives are retained | Saved rankings were assessed at the higher threshold without refitting | Missed high-density dives, low-density and ghost dives avoided, and intermediate dives retained |
| Which manta tows to omit | Recorded surveys were thinned while keeping the same number of tows for each strategy | Habitat-ranked, random and evenly spaced tows; observed aggregations still detected |

: Evaluation of the tactical decisions. The season-by-season evidence model used earlier outcomes, but its habitat models were withheld by reef and were not also restricted to earlier years. {#tbl-evaluation-purpose}


The main Methods define each model by its purpose. This appendix retains the
implementation detail needed to reproduce it. Original software labels are used
in archived tables and figure legends; their meanings are mapped below.

| Original label | Description used in the main report |
|---|---|
| clean + year | Annual full-extent model (13 predictors) |
| RG + year | Annual limited-extent model (18 predictors) |
| manta / manta with year | Annual habitat model fitted to manta observations |
| manta within reef-year | Manta habitat model accounting for differences among reef-years |
| combined site ranking | Recent-evidence site ranking |
| HMSC joint | Multi-observation habitat model |
| HMSC + history | Habitat updated by longer cull history; distinct from the operational site ranking |

: Model purposes and evaluation design. {#tbl-supplement-1}


The habitat-model reporting follows the Overview, Data, Model, Assessment and Prediction (ODMAP) protocol for species distribution models [@zurell2020odmap]. This structure specifies the management question and prediction target, the observations and predictors used, the model fitting, how predictions are evaluated, and how the resulting maps should be used. The sections below describe these elements for the habitat and search-ranking analyses; the metacommunity methods describe the population model, calibration and prescribed culling separately.

### Data and response definitions {.unnumbered}

The COTS Control Program's full cull dataset covered 2002–2026 and supplied the site, date, number of COTS culled and bottom time for each dive. Records with missing counts or non-positive bottom time were excluded. Records matched to designated cull sites covered `r int(crscope$matched_sites)` sites on `r int(crscope$matched_reefs)` reefs; the wider cleaned dataset contained records from `r int(crscope$all_record_reefs)` reefs. The archived habitat fits used the full-period source dataset, while each validation applied its stated spatial and temporal subsets. [TO CONFIRM: data-access agreement.]
<!-- Full source-period coverage confirmed by the author in review 03, comment 41.
Matching details are retained in R/cull_sites.R and scripts 15–17, not repeated
in the narrative; numerical sample scope comes from script 23. -->

Two CPUE thresholds serve different purposes. The archived habitat fits and original validation defined a problematic dive as CPUE ≥0.02 COTS per minute of bottom time. A ghost dive found no COTS; a low-density dive found COTS at positive CPUE <0.02. This lower threshold identifies dives that might be avoided while retaining some control below the ecological management target. The revised management evaluation instead penalises missed dives above 0.04. Dives from 0.02 to 0.04 inclusive form an intermediate group of useful culling opportunities. Their retention is reported separately, while missed >0.04 dives remain the primary omission measure. Thus exactly 0.02 remains positive under the original response and belongs to the intermediate group in the new evaluation; exactly 0.04 also belongs to the intermediate group. Ecologically sustainable densities vary with coral cover, so 0.04 is the operational criterion for this assessment, rather than a universal coral-growth threshold [@plaganyi2020targets]. Habitat fits used a site-year response, while search selection was assessed against individual dive outcomes. The two thresholds do not change the definition of a manta aggregation.

The habitat model fitted to manta observations used `r int(mt("within", "auc", col = "tows"))` labelled tows in `r int(mt("within", "auc", col = "reef_years"))` reef-years, including `r int(mt("within", "auc", col = "strong_tows"))` with strong COTS evidence. Strong evidence meant a direct COTS sighting, at least two counted feeding scars, or scars recorded as “common” in legacy surveys. Strict negatives recorded neither COTS nor scars; weak single-scar records were excluded from model fitting. The observation archives included Control Program crews (2016 onward), the Reef Joint Field Management Program (2012 onward) and AIMS LTMP (1992 onward), as specified by the author. SALAD [@pratchett2022salad] and RHIS [@beeden2014rhis] observations contributed to the joint habitat model. ReefScan imagery [@bainbridge2024reefscan] supplied a separate presence-only check in script 10 and was not a fitted response in the delivered joint model.

Predictors were assembled on a 30 m grid in GDA2020 / MGA zone 55. The clean stack contained depth, slope, eastness, northness, bathymetric position index, vector ruggedness, sky-view factor, horizontal and vertical curvature, and three coral habitat-suitability surfaces for *Acropora* taxa [@guillaume2025coral]. Five ReefGuide layers added significant wave height, wave period, turbidity, bathymetry and slope. The joint model also used geomorphic classes and reef features. Appendix B lists predictor codes. Sources: @gbrmpabathymetry2021, @gbrmpageomorphic2021, @roelfsema2021shallow and @reefguide2026. ReefGuide coverage was reduced in some deeper areas, particularly beyond about 15–20 m. [TO CONFIRM: predictor product versions and resampling methods.]

### Habitat models and mapped layers {.unnumbered}

The clean + year model used gradient-boosted trees [XGBoost; @chen2016xgboost] to predict the problematic-density indicator from the clean stack and survey year. The RG + year model added the five ReefGuide predictors. These cull-trained models learned from locations selected by crews, often following manta evidence, so their scores reflect the program's sampling footprint as well as habitat. The operational refits used 1,500 boosting rounds, a learning rate of 0.00137382379588326, maximum tree depth 5, minimum child weight 20 and gamma $10^{-10}$, retaining the archived hyperparameters. These settings were not retuned on the evaluation reefs.

The primary search-planning layer used RG + year where available and clean + year elsewhere, calibrated onto the RG probability scale before combining them. Each 30 m cell was then ranked within its reef polygon, with map priority classes for the top 10%, 10–20% and 20–30%. RG + year covered `r p0(pick(lcov, layer_id = "legacy_rg_year2026", col = "fraction"))` of the reef-polygon support cells used in the coverage analysis. Of the mapped reefs, `r int(sum(rsrc$source == "RG only"))` used RG alone, `r int(sum(rsrc$source == "mixed"))` mixed the two sources and `r int(sum(rsrc$source == "clean fallback only"))` used the clean fallback alone.

Manta-trained XGBoost models used the RG stack and the same boosting settings. Predictor values were averaged along each tow. A model with survey year was compared with a model designed specifically to rank locations within reef-years. For the latter, the logit of the reef-year's strong-tow proportion, with a half-count correction, entered training as a fixed offset and survey year was omitted. The offset was omitted when predicting relative habitat scores because it was constant within a reef-year. The resulting map represents relative log-odds, not an annual occurrence probability. The cull-trained and manta-trained ranks were also compared as an average rank and as separate terms in the evidence model.

The hierarchical model of species communities [HMSC; @ovaskainen2017hmsc; @tikhonov2020hmsc] related cull, SALAD and RHIS responses jointly to habitat at 120 m, conditional on an active reef-year. Three predictor components supplied fallbacks where enhanced predictors were unavailable. Production fits used four chains, each retaining 1,000 samples at thinning 30 after 5,000 transient iterations. Convergence was assessed against a minimum effective sample size of 400 and maximum upper potential scale reduction factor of 1.1 (Appendix C). This model supplied explanatory habitat effects and uncertainty.

An additional layer represented known aggregation sites using a Gaussian kernel of the problematic rate in earlier active cull site-years (σ = 500 m). Its rate *H* and evidence weight *W* updated the HMSC habitat probability *p* as (κ*p* + *WH*)/(κ + *W*), with κ = 2 for the fixed-setting comparison. History and dive effort were interpreted as records of past finds and crew targeting, rather than independent habitat evidence.

### How habitat and recent observations determine a cull-site rank {.unnumbered}

The main Methods gives the score equation. The fitted response was whether a dive reached CPUE ≥0.02; reassessment at >0.04 changed the evaluation target, not this model. The habitat term $H_i$ was the mean deployed habitat score over a site's polygon, converted to a percentile among designated sites on the reef. A missing habitat rank was replaced by 0.5. The operational product used the cull-trained habitat layer with its full-extent fallback, without a second manta-habitat term.

Recent dive and tow records were represented at dive coordinates and tow midpoints. Missing dive coordinates used a representative point inside the matched site. For site $i$ and nearby record $j$, the spatial weight was:

$$
w_{ij}=\begin{cases}
\exp\left[-d_{ij}^{2}/\{2(300\,\mathrm{m})^{2}\}\right], & d_{ij}\leq900\,\mathrm{m},\\
0, & d_{ij}>900\,\mathrm{m}.
\end{cases}
$$

Distances were measured from the site's representative interior point in GDA2020 / MGA zone 55. The calculation considered at most the 400 nearest records in each data stream. $E_i=\sum_j w_{ij}$ was the weighted number of dive records, not minutes of bottom time. $R_i=\sum_j w_{ij}y_j/E_i$, where $y_j=1$ for CPUE ≥0.02, was their weighted positive proportion. The analogous tow sums supplied $T_i$ for all records and $M_i$ for strong evidence (a direct COTS sighting, multiple counted scars or legacy common scars). Searches with no strong evidence contributed to effort but not to the positive sum. There was no additional age weighting within the evidence window.

The direct-site indicators were $P_i=1$ if any recent dive assigned to that site reached ≥0.02, and $Q_i=1$ if the site was dived but none reached that threshold. Both were zero for an undived site. Where no nearby dives were available, $R_i$ and $E_i$ were zero; absent tows gave $M_i=T_i=0$. With no recent evidence, the score therefore reduced to the intercept plus habitat term. No evidence was treated differently from a searched site with a quiet result.

The coefficients were estimated jointly by logistic regression. They are conditional associations, not independent bonuses or penalties. @tbl-ranking-coefficients records the final 2027 coefficients; the forward evaluation estimated a different coefficient set using only years preceding each test year.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-ranking-coefficients
#| tbl-cap: "Coefficients used in the 2027 cull-site score, fitted to the archived ≥0.02 dive response. Inputs and transformations match the score equation in Methods. These coefficients describe the deployed fit, not the separately fitted forward-validation years."
rank_terms <- c("(Intercept)","habitat","site_problematic_prev","site_quiet_prev","cull_rate","log_cull_effort","log_manta_strong","log_manta_effort")
stopifnot(identical(as.character(src$term),rank_terms))
knitr::kable(data.frame(Input=c("Intercept","Within-reef habitat rank","Any ≥0.02 dive at this site","Dived here, none ≥0.02","Nearby ≥0.02 dive proportion","log(1 + weighted dive count)","log(1 + weighted strong tow count)","log(1 + weighted total tow count)"),
 Symbol=c("β₀","βH","βP","βQ","βR","βE","βM","βT"),Coefficient=num(src$estimate,3),check.names=FALSE),row.names=FALSE)
```

The logistic transform $p_i=1/(1+\exp[-s_i])$ expresses the fitted probability of a ≥0.02 outcome conditional on diving there. Rankings use $s_i$, so the transform does not change their order. This is not a probability of an irruption or of presence at an unvisited site. In the deployed product, sites are sorted from highest to lowest score on each reef, using higher cull-habitat rank to break score ties. Descending rank divided by the reef's site count defines A (≤0.2), B (>0.2 to 0.5), C (>0.5 to 0.8) and D (>0.8); retaining A–C selects floor(0.8 × site count). Pop-up evidence labels describe the records; they do not override the fitted score. Historical evaluation retains the archived random tie order.

For validation, prior evidence came from the preceding calendar season. The 2027 product instead used the latest complete 365-day window, 1 June 2025–31 May 2026, and coefficients fitted on `r int(src$training_dives[1])` dives from `r src$training_years[1]`. The search tool is therefore a habitat ranking updated with both positive and negative operational evidence, and its effort terms also encode where crews chose to work.

### Evaluation design and search-efficiency analyses {.unnumbered}

Operational discrimination was measured among locations on the same reef in the same year. Within reef-year AUC compared positive and negative locations only within those groups; an AUC of 0.5 indicated no discrimination. Top-20% lift was the share of positives in the highest-ranked fifth divided by 0.2. These metrics were supplemented by the outcomes retained when effort was reduced.

For operational habitat comparisons, reefs were assigned to five folds and every reef was scored by a model refitted without any reefs in its fold [@roberts2017cv]. The pipeline calls this leave-reef-out validation; it is grouped five-fold validation, rather than one refit per reef. This prevented a reef's cull or manta observations from contributing to its habitat fit. A separate matched manta check scored the same `r int(mi("RG + year", "tows"))` tows in `r int(mi("RG + year", "reef_years"))` active reef-years on `r int(mi("RG + year", "reefs"))` reefs where all deployed layers were available. That check used the fitted layers and was not a substitute for the refitted operational evaluation.

Manta aggregations were connected groups of strong-evidence tow midpoints linked within 500 m in a survey (reef and date); successive links could join a group wider than 500 m. The principal aggregation analysis required at least two strong tows, with isolated records examined separately. Surveys required at least five scored tows and some strong evidence. An aggregation was retained if at least one of its tows was kept. This measured retention of observed aggregation evidence under retrospective thinning.

Each thinning strategy kept the same number of tows per survey, over retained shares from 90% to 30%. Model thinning kept the highest-scoring tows. Random thinning used the exact hypergeometric expectation of retaining at least one tow in each aggregation. Systematic thinning kept evenly spaced positions in the tow sequence, averaged over 20 starting offsets. Recorded tow order was unavailable, so sequence was approximated by bearing from the survey centre. The comparison therefore concerned thinning existing surveillance, not the performance of newly designed tow routes.

Cull-site analyses ranked every designated site on a reef, including never-dived sites, by its mean habitat score over the polygon. For each retained share of designated sites, the analysis recorded the share of observed problematic, low-density and ghost dives at retained sites. Random selection supplied a no-information expectation: retaining a fraction of sites gives that fraction's expected retention of each observed outcome. Outcomes at never-dived sites were unknown, so this exercise could not measure COTS missed at those sites or changes in crew behaviour under deployment.

To add recent evidence, each site received indicators for any problematic dive there in the previous season and for having been dived with none problematic. Neighbourhood terms were the problematic rate and dive effort among nearby cull dives, and strong-evidence and total manta tows, using a Gaussian kernel with σ = 300 m. Effort and tow counts entered logistic regressions after log(1 + *x*) transformation; missing habitat ranks were assigned the midpoint. Habitat alone, evidence alone, habitat + evidence and a simple flagged-sites-first rule were compared. The regressions were fitted on other reef folds, and evidence for a test year came only from preceding seasons. This spatial test did not also restrict regression training outcomes to years before the test year.

Rankings were compared at matched retention of problematic dives because evidence could move both problematic and low-density dives upwards. Retention curves were evaluated over 5% steps in designated sites searched and interpolated at 80%, 85%, 90% and 95% problematic-dive retention. The separate season-by-season test used 80% and 90%. For each test year from 2019 to 2026, its evidence regression was fitted only on earlier dive outcomes, comparing all earlier seasons with the last five or three, and cull-only, averaged cull–manta or separate habitat terms. Habitat covariates in this test were the reef-held-out ranks from the spatial analysis; the habitat fits themselves were not restricted to preceding years. Thus the evidence regression was tested forward in time, while the habitat component was held out spatially.

The >0.04 reassessment kept the saved rankings from the habitat-only, recent-evidence and manta-habitat comparisons and the season-by-season evidence test; none was refitted to the higher threshold. Dive counts and CPUE were rejoined to the saved scores using reef, year and designated site. For the forward test, the recovered dive counts and original outcome classes were checked against the saved evaluation sample, preventing repeated dives at one site from generating duplicated records. The candidate set remained every designated site on each evaluated reef, including never-dived sites. At each rank cutoff, effort was the actual number of designated site-years selected, summed across evaluated reef-years, divided by all candidate site-years. Consequently the proportion searched could differ slightly from the nominal cutoff on reefs with few sites or tied habitat ranks.

The reassessment reported retention and omission of >0.04 dives, low-density and ghost dives avoided, and intermediate dives retained. Random selection used the exact expected outcomes for the same number of sites on each reef; it matched the combined ranking's effort in the spatial comparison and all rankings' effort in the forward comparison. Curves were also interpolated at 80%, 90%, 95% and 99% retention of >0.04 dives, using the first crossing of each target over 5% rank-cutoff steps. This interpolation describes a trade-off between adjacent effort levels, rather than a validated stopping rule for an individual reef. Confidence intervals used 500 paired reef-year bootstrap draws for this reassessment, including the forward scores. Earlier ≥0.02 results retain their original calculations and bootstrap counts. The high-density reassessment retains the original spatial and temporal holdout limits of each ranking.

Site-selection counts describe candidate locations for cull dives; tow effort, dive effort and annual coverage are separate quantities. For the exact operational cutoff we retained sites with descending rank divided by the number of sites on the reef ≤0.8, matching classes A–C in the delivered product. This selects floor(0.8 × site count) sites per reef and can differ from the percentile interpolation used for the matched-retention rows. The saved forward coefficients and original random tie sequence reproduced every archived dive rank exactly; no model was refitted. Historical ties retain the forward test's random order; the deployed product uses habitat as a tie-breaker. The retrospective habitat component retained its spatial holdout, while the evidence regression used earlier years. The 2027 map itself uses the deployed habitat layer and latest evidence, rather than those validation fits.

The manta-effort estimate used recorded tows on the same evaluated reef-years. Valid start and end coordinates defined straight segments, projected to GDA2020 / MGA zone 55; source geometry fallbacks and zero-length segments were excluded. Each segment was split at designated-site boundaries. A portion could be deferred only if it lay within designated sites and all sites sharing that portion were deferred. Parts outside designated sites remained surveyed. The whole-tow metric counted only segments entirely deferred; the distance metric summed deferred portions and divided by total valid segment length. Repeated surveys contributed their recorded effort. No buffer was added around site polygons, and endpoints did not reconstruct the actual curved vessel track.

For random selection, exact probabilities that none of a portion's overlapping sites was selected supplied the expected deferred distance; whole-tow omission used the union of sites along a segment. The random comparison selected the same integer count of sites on each reef. The matched-retention tow estimates used the same percentile cutoffs and first-crossing interpolation as the existing dive curves. A separate set of 500 paired reef-year bootstrap draws propagated cull outcomes, site counts and tow effort together. These estimates describe spatial scope for reducing recorded surveillance conditional on still diving selected sites. No causal tow-to-dive detection model, route feasibility or vessel-time saving was inferred. All site-years contributed to the dive and site metrics; only reef-years with valid tow segments contributed to the tow denominators.

A field trial will record tows and their duration, dives and bottom time, COTS outcomes, added exploration searches, departures from the proposed search order, and later checks of deferred sites. It will compare the ranking with crews' normal planning. Sites deferred on a visit will still be checked annually or before the reef closes to further control visits. Analyses of the full season must count those later checks and added exploration, so that shifting effort between sites or visits is distinguished from reducing total vessel and diver time. Existing records cannot estimate outcomes at unvisited sites or the yield of the proposed new routes.

The HMSC–history forecast used a separate temporal design: for each test year from 2022 to 2026, habitat models were refitted on earlier years and history used earlier active site-years only. First-visit cull site-years were compared within reef-years containing both outcomes, using habitat, prior dive effort, history and their blend. This distinguished habitat transfer from the persistence of previous finds.

Uncertainty intervals used paired bootstrap resamples of reef-years for tow and cull metrics, or surveys for aggregation retention. Operational spatial comparisons used 500 resamples; the season-by-season site-ranking test used 200. The same resampled units were used across scores to preserve paired comparisons.

### Seasonal products {.unnumbered}

For 2027, the selected cull-habitat + evidence model was fitted on `r int(src$training_dives[1])` dives from `r src$training_years[1]`. Recent evidence covered 1 June 2025 to 31 May 2026, the latest 12 months available, because calendar 2026 contained only January–May. Sites were ranked within reefs and assigned classes A (top 20%), B (20–50%), C (50–80%) and D (bottom 20%). The deployed habitat layer supplied scores for this product; the operational validation used refitted habitat scores.

Exploration areas were drawn from 30 m cells 0.5–16 m deep in the reef's top 30% of habitat, more than 100 m from designated cull sites and more than 150 m from manta tows in the preceding five seasons. Habitat was the mean of the primary-layer and manta-model percentiles, re-ranked within the reef, with the primary layer alone where manta scores were missing. Nearby pockets were joined, large patches split into compact areas of about 9 ha, and outlines smoothed and clipped to the reef outside cull sites. Areas smaller than 0.5 ha were removed; up to ten areas per reef polygon, at least 350 m apart, were retained. These areas identified places to explore beyond the recent search footprint.

### Metacommunity model and historical culling {.unnumbered}

The detailed calibration and spatial-kernel removal specification below records the 15 October setup. Appendix I describes the subsequent changes to settlement, coral settings, reef-wide removal allocation and effort-based projections used in the current Results.

The strategic modelling strand extended COTSMod [@matthews2020cotsmod] through the Julia package COTSMod.jl, coupled to ADRIA and the CoralBlox coral model [@cotsmodmethods2026; @adriamethods2026; @dealmeida2026coralblox]. COTSMod.jl supplied population transitions, coral predation and larval processes; ADRIA supplied the spatial domain, disturbance forcing and scenario execution. The prototype used the Lizard Island cluster, with 2,895 sub-reef sites on 113 reefs. Historical simulations beginning in 1991 were assessed against AIMS Long-Term Monitoring Program (LTMP) manta COTS and coral records on Lizard Island, Eyrie, MacGillivray and North Direction reefs. The model state was expressed as recruit, juvenile and adult densities per hectare of site area, with coral cover represented relative to habitable area.

Site-level habitable fractions came from benthic maps in domain v0.3 and its v0.4 extension. Historical heat stress was supplied through ADRIA, with cyclone exposure examined as an option. Reef-to-reef larval flows were divided evenly among sites within a receiving reef. Habitable fractions and prescribed removals varied among sites, but transport did not yet resolve within-reef flows. The 30 m habitat layers and evidence-based search rankings were candidate inputs for future coupling, rather than validated components of the metacommunity model. [TO CONFIRM: source and attribution of the annual 2018–2022 connectivity matrices, status and delivery date of Work Plan output F, and the planned coupling to the habitat layers.]

The working COTS formulation combined preferred-first per-capita grazing, survival linked to remembered preferred coral cover, adult senescence and preferred-food effects on reproductive condition. Larval production included a low-density Allee effect, juvenile survival included a saturating predator-pit term, and larvae were transported using reef-level connectivity and supplied from outside the domain. External supply was derived from the reef-level irruption-probability hindcast [@stewart2026hybrid]; its production multiplier was a calibration assumption, not measured recruitment. Mechanisms suggested by MICE, CoCoNet and ReefMod-GBR were examined as optional alternatives [@morello2014model; @plaganyi2020targets; @condie2021interventions; @bozec2022cumulative]. Testing a mechanism did not make it part of the working configuration. [TO CONFIRM: attribution and final choice of the annual connectivity matrices; the sub-reef hydrodynamic network had not replaced these reef-level inputs.]

Calibration used bounded comparisons of candidate mechanisms and parameter settings. Each screen was preregistered, included an exact-replay reference and recorded settings, seeds, input checksums and repository revisions. Candidate mechanisms had to pass a qualitative peak-and-trough gate before wider optimisation. Irruption peak presence, timing and height, inter-irruption troughs and coral trajectories were assessed together. Coral dynamics were also assessed with COTS grazing forced from observed records to separate coral-model errors from population-dynamics errors. Simulated adult density was converted to manta CPUE through an explicit observation model. The working linear conversion used *CPUE* = *qA*, with *A* in adults ha$^{-1}$ and *q* = 0.015 COTS tow$^{-1}$ per adult ha$^{-1}$; alternative scales and density-dependent detection, *CPUE* = *qA*²/(*A* + *A*½), were sensitivity analyses. These alternatives were kept distinct because they change both initial-density estimates and the comparison with observations. In-sample calibration and diagnostic screens were not treated as held-out validation or evidence of management benefit.

The replicated historical comparison used score v2, which scored North Direction against its raw series and omitted Eyrie's unobserved first wave from the peak count. Its three retained candidates were compared over five recorded seed pairs. The later v0.4 diagnostic extended forcing to 2026 and used score v3: the manta-based score on 1992–2021 plus 1.5 times a diver-anchored recent-density log error. Original and cull/SALAD-corrected irruption boundaries were crossed with earlier and revised coral thermal settings; exploratory chlorophyll-derived larval-survival modifiers were also screened. These later runs used one seed pair and prescribed culling was off. Their corrected boundary and recent-density score shared evidence, so the comparison was a diagnostic fit rather than a validation. The two score versions were reported separately.

Observed historical culling was included as prescribed removals. Cull records from the licensed CSIRO compilation were retained for reefs in the domain, grouped by site and year, and mapped to model sites on the same reef. Counts were distributed with weights proportional to site area × exp(−*d*²/(2σ²)) within 3σ of the cull-site centroid, normalised to preserve total counts. The primary width was σ = 210 m, with nearest-site allocation (σ = 0) and σ = 420 m as sensitivities; the nearest site was used if no centroid lay within the kernel. Allocated counts were divided by model-site area to obtain removals in COTS ha$^{-1}$. COTS below 15 cm were assigned to the juvenile stage and those at least 15 cm to adults, an explicit size-to-stage approximation.

September–December removals were assigned to the following LTMP reporting year and applied before spawning; January–August removals were applied after spawning in their reporting year. The annual implementation placed these removals immediately before or after the COTS predation and population-transition call. Requested removals were capped at the simulated juvenile or adult population present, recruits were left unchanged, and adult age and size substates were scaled by the surviving adult fraction. The model logged actual removals separately from requested removals, allowing a shortage of simulated COTS to be diagnosed rather than removing animals that were absent.

This culling implementation prescribed observed catches. It did not yet predict diver search, catchability, effort costs or adaptive starting and stopping decisions. The intended scenarios—primary irruption suppression, starting and stopping rules, and downstream consequences—require further calibration and independent validation before their management performance can be assessed.

#### Design of the historical and future control assessments {.unnumbered}

The intended historical assessment pairs simulations with recorded removals from 2012 onward and simulations without program removals, starting from the same pre-control population and coral state and using matching environmental sequences and random seeds. Outcomes will include actual removals, infeasible requested removals, COTS abundance, larval export, cumulative coral consumption and coral cover. Holding external larval supply identical estimates the effect of control within the model domain conditional on unchanged outside reefs. A regional no-culling assessment instead requires an external supply history consistent with no control outside the domain. This experiment is a planned extension of the prescribed-removal diagnostics reported here; no completed paired program-impact estimate is asserted.

Future comparisons will examine stopping when local coral protection is no longer achievable versus continuing to reduce larval export, and when to begin or intensify control on reefs whose COTS populations cannot be reduced below a local target. Reallocation within existing vessel capacity and additional capacity will be compared separately, using current control and no control as references. Feasible removals must follow population availability and an effort–catchability relationship, rather than prescribed catches alone. Each paired comparison will share climate, disturbance and random-seed sequences, and repeat across plausible population, coral, connectivity and observation assumptions. Local and downstream coral outcomes and the resources required for fifth-wave suppression will be reported together. [TO CONFIRM: final effort–catchability model, projection horizon, vessel budgets, intervention rules and climate scenarios agreed with partners.]

### Software and reproducibility {.unnumbered}

The SDM analyses used R 4.5.0 with xgboost, Hmsc and terra. Inputs were pinned by SHA-256 checksum in the final pipeline configuration, and reported results were read from output tables when the documents were rendered. [TO CONFIRM: package versions for the archived fits and a release identifier for the final analysis.] Metacommunity methods were checked against local COTSMod.jl and ADRIA code on 15 October 2026. The citations record both repository revisions and declare the uncommitted ADRIA changes inspected for this pass. [TO CONFIRM: Julia and package versions and the frozen code release to accompany submission.]

## Appendix H: Detailed tactical model comparisons {.unnumbered}

### Full cull-site and manta-effort trade-offs {.unnumbered}

The four mutually exclusive dive classes complete the accounting for the exact A–C cutoff (@tbl-deferred-counts). Counts describe observed dives at selected or deferred sites, including repeated visits. Random values are exact expected counts under the same number of candidate sites selected on each reef; they need not be integers. @tbl-operational-highlights in the main Results reports retention, avoidance and deferred-dive composition with paired reef-year intervals. Those percentages have different denominators and must not be added across those three groups.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-deferred-counts
#| tbl-cap: "Observed dive counts and the dives deferred by the exact A–C rule, 2019–2026. Intermediate dives remain useful culling opportunities. Random selection uses the same candidate-site count, rather than the same observed dive count."
ob <- opbreakdown[match(c("ghost","low","intermediate","high"),opbreakdown$band),]
knitr::kable(data.frame(`Dive class`=c("Ghost: CPUE = 0","Low: 0 < CPUE <0.02","Intermediate: 0.02 ≤ CPUE ≤0.04","High: CPUE >0.04"),
 `All observed dives`=int(ob$observed_dives),`Ranking: deferred dives`=int(ob$deferred_dives),
 `Random: expected deferred dives`=num(ob$random_deferred_dives,1),check.names=FALSE),row.names=FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-search-highlights
#| tbl-cap: "Cull sites selected for dives and low-density or ghost dives avoided, 2019–2026. Upper rows fix retention of >0.04 CPUE dives; final rows fix the A–C site count and report retention. Percentages [95% reef-year bootstrap intervals]. Sites are candidate site-years, including never-dived sites, rather than confirmed culling visits. Low-density means positive CPUE <0.02; ghost means zero; intermediate dives (0.02–0.04 inclusive) are separate. Appendix G gives validation details; @tbl-manta-effort gives manta effort. Annual follow-up is excluded."
highlight_rows <- expand.grid(target = c(0.8, 0.9, 0.95, 0.99), score = c("habitat", "combined", "random"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
highlight_rows <- highlight_rows[order(highlight_rows$target, highlight_rows$score), ]
highlight_metric <- function(metric) vapply(seq_len(nrow(highlight_rows)), function(i) {
  x <- highlight_rows[i, ]
  sprintf("%.1f [%.1f–%.1f]", 100 * hd(metric, x$target, x$score),
    100 * hd(metric, x$target, x$score, col = "low"), 100 * hd(metric, x$target, x$score, col = "high"))
}, character(1))
highlight_table <- data.frame(
  `High-density retained (%)` = as.character(100 * highlight_rows$target),
  Ranking = c(combined = "Habitat + recent observations", habitat = "Habitat alone", random = "Random selection")[highlight_rows$score],
  `Sites selected for cull dives (%)` = highlight_metric("sites_searched"),
  `Low-density avoided (%)` = highlight_metric("low_avoided"),
  `Ghost dives avoided (%)` = highlight_metric("ghost_avoided"),
  check.names = FALSE)
opsc <- c("combined", "habitat", "random")
opcell <- function(metric) vapply(opsc, function(s) sprintf("%.1f [%.1f–%.1f]", 100 * oc(metric, s), 100 * oc(metric, s, "low"), 100 * oc(metric, s, "high")), "")
operational_rows <- data.frame(opcell("high_retained"),
  c("A–C: habitat + recent observations", "A–C count: habitat alone", "A–C count: random selection"),
  opcell("sites_selected"), opcell("low_avoided"), opcell("ghost_avoided"), check.names = FALSE)
names(operational_rows) <- names(highlight_table)
knitr::kable(rbind(highlight_table, operational_rows), row.names = FALSE)
```

Shading shows 95% reef-year bootstrap intervals; dotted horizontal lines mark 80%, 90%, 95% and 99% retention. The diamond marks the exact A–C cutoff used for the priority classes in @fig-2027 and the final rows of @tbl-search-highlights. Habitat fits were held out by reef, while the evidence regression used earlier seasons. ```{r}
#| label: tbl-manta-effort
#| tbl-cap: "Potential manta-surveillance reductions paired with @tbl-search-highlights, before annual checks or exploration. Upper rows use the stated dive-retention targets; final rows fix the A–C site count. Percentages [95% reef-year bootstrap intervals] refer to whole recorded tows or total straight-line segment distance. Surveillance outside designated sites and in overlaps with retained sites remains. These spatial effort proxies assume retained cull visits still occur; detection after tow removal, route feasibility and time savings are untested."
manta_rows <- data.frame(Rule = paste0(c(80,90,95,99), "% dive retention"),

  vals <- vapply(c(.8,.9,.95,.99), function(t) sprintf("%.1f [%.1f–%.1f]", 100 * om(metric,t), 100 * om(metric,t,col="low"), 100 * om(metric,t,col="high")), "")
  manta_rows[[metric]] <- vals
}
manta_op <- data.frame(Rule = "A–C site count", Ranking = c("Habitat + recent observations", "Habitat alone", "Random selection"),
  manta_tows_avoided = opcell("manta_tows_avoided"), manta_distance_avoided = opcell("manta_distance_avoided"))
manta_table <- rbind(manta_rows, manta_op)
names(manta_table)[3:4] <- c("Whole manta tows avoided (%)", "Manta tow distance avoided (%)")

### Recent evidence combined with habitat reduces the cull-site search {.unnumbered}

In the original ≥0.02 evaluation, ranking designated cull sites by last season's cull dives and manta tows, with the habitat layer ordering sites that lack recent evidence, reduced the search needed for the same problematic dives (@tbl-evidence, @fig-evidence). The ranking is a logistic model fitted on other reefs (leave-reef-out) that uses evidence from the previous season only, never from the season being searched. Held out over 2018–2026 (`r int(ev_dives)` dives in `r int(ev_ry)` reef-years), with 90% of problematic dives retained, the combined ranking:

- reduced the designated sites searched from `r p0(ev("sites_searched", 0.9, "habitat"))` to `r p0(ev("sites_searched", 0.9, "combined"))`;
- raised low-density dives avoided from `r p0(ev("low_dives_avoided", 0.9, "habitat"))` to `r p0(ev("low_dives_avoided", 0.9, "combined"))`;
- raised ghost dives avoided from `r p0(ev("ghost_dives_avoided", 0.9, "habitat"))` to `r p0(ev("ghost_dives_avoided", 0.9, "combined"))`.

All paired bootstrap intervals excluded zero. Gains were larger in recent seasons. In 2022–2026, keeping 80% of problematic dives needed `r p0(ev("sites_searched", 0.8, "combined", "2022-2026"))` of designated sites instead of `r p0(ev("sites_searched", 0.8, "habitat", "2022-2026"))`. Low-density dives avoided rose from `r p0(ev("low_dives_avoided", 0.8, "habitat", "2022-2026"))` to `r p0(ev("low_dives_avoided", 0.8, "combined", "2022-2026"))`.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-evidence
#| tbl-cap: "Habitat-only ranking → habitat plus previous-season evidence, compared at matched retention of problematic dives (CPUE ≥0.02; held out). Brackets: 95% paired bootstrap interval of the difference, in percentage points."
cell <- function(metric, r, period) sprintf("%s → %s (%s)", p0(ev(metric, r, "habitat", period)), p0(ev(metric, r, "combined", period)),
  gpp(ev(metric, r, "combined", period, "gain_low"), ev(metric, r, "combined", period, "gain_high")))
rows <- expand.grid(r = c(0.9, 0.8), period = c("2018-2026", "2022-2026"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Period = sub("-", "–", rows$period),
  `Problematic dives kept` = p0(rows$r),
  `Designated sites searched` = mapply(cell, "sites_searched", rows$r, rows$period),
  `Low-density dives avoided` = mapply(cell, "low_dives_avoided", rows$r, rows$period),
  `Ghost dives avoided` = mapply(cell, "ghost_dives_avoided", rows$r, rows$period),
  check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE, align = "lllll")
```

![Habitat-only and evidence-informed rankings of designated cull sites compared at the same share of problematic dives retained (80–95%). Panels: share of designated sites searched (lower is better), and shares of low-density and ghost dives avoided. Evidence is from the previous season only. Bars are 95% bootstrap intervals over reef-years (2018–2026). Adding last season's evidence shifts every curve in the useful direction.](../outputs/figures/fig15_cull_search_area_evidence.png){#fig-evidence width="100%"}

The fitted model weighs the evidence in ways that match field experience:

- strong manta tows or problematic dives nearby raised a site's rank;
- a site dived the previous season with nothing problematic dropped sharply;
- a site that had itself been problematic ranked slightly lower than its neighbourhood suggested, consistent with culling having reduced it.

Most of the reduction came from ranking quiet and never-dived sites lower. Among dives actually made, discrimination between problematic and low-density dives rose only from `r a2(pick(eauc, window = "last_season", subset = "all", score = "habitat", col = "auc_problematic_vs_low"))` to `r a2(pick(eauc, window = "last_season", subset = "all", score = "combined", col = "auc_problematic_vs_low"))`.

A simple rule ("last season's flagged sites first, then habitat") searched the fewest sites but avoided fewer low-density dives than the fitted model. A three-season evidence window gave the same picture.

### The gain holds season by season {.unnumbered}

The evidence model was also tested using earlier seasons to predict later ones. Its habitat models were withheld by reef but were not restricted to earlier years. It avoided more low-density dives than habitat alone in every season from 2022, and searched fewer sites in every season from 2023 (@tbl-seasons). It did not help in 2019–2021, when fewer earlier seasons were available to learn from.

Pooled over 2019–2026 (`r int(fw_dives)` dives in `r int(fw_ry)` reef-years), with 90% of problematic dives retained, sites searched fell from `r p0(fw("habitat_only", "sites_searched_at_90"))` to `r p0(fw("cull_all", "sites_searched_at_90"))`. Low-density dives avoided rose from `r p0(fw("habitat_only", "low_dives_avoided_at_90"))` to `r p0(fw("cull_all", "low_dives_avoided_at_90"))`. Training on all earlier seasons matched the last five (`r p0(fw("cull_last5", "sites_searched_at_90"))` of sites) and outperformed the last three (`r p0(fw("cull_last3", "sites_searched_at_90"))`). Adding the manta model to the habitat term made no difference (`r p0(fw("ensemble_all", "sites_searched_at_90"))`), so the simpler cull-trained habitat term was kept.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-seasons
#| tbl-cap: "Year-by-year forward test of the cull-site ranking with 90% of problematic dives (CPUE ≥0.02) retained. Each season uses an evidence model fitted only on earlier seasons, with habitat models withheld by reef. Values are habitat alone → cull-trained habitat + last season's evidence (all earlier seasons)."
periods <- c(as.character(2019:2026), "2019-2026")
lab <- c(as.character(2019:2025), "2026 (Jan–May)", "2019–2026")
arrow <- function(p, metric, f = p0) sprintf("%s → %s", f(fw("habitat_only", metric, p)), f(fw("cull_all", metric, p)))
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  `Test season` = lab,
  Dives = vapply(periods, function(p) int(fw("cull_all", "sites_searched_at_90", p, "dives")), ""),
  `Cull sites selected` = vapply(periods, arrow, "", metric = "sites_searched_at_90"),
  `Low-density dives avoided` = vapply(periods, arrow, "", metric = "low_dives_avoided_at_90"),
  `AUC, problematic vs low-density` = vapply(periods, arrow, "", metric = "auc_problematic_vs_low", f = a2),
  check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE, align = "lrlll")
```

A caveat applies to all cull-site results. A ranking is credited when it agrees with where crews chose to dive. Crews already use the previous season's knowledge, so part of the gain formalises current practice. COTS densities at designated sites that were never dived cannot be verified from these data.

### Retaining dives above 0.04 CPUE {.unnumbered}

Re-evaluating the unchanged rankings against dives above 0.04 CPUE showed how the acceptable omission rate constrains search reductions (@tbl-high-density, @fig-high-density). In the forward evidence test over 2019–2026, retaining 95% of these dives required searching `r hdci("sites_searched")` of designated site-years with the combined ranking, compared with `r hdci("sites_searched", score = "habitat")` using habitat alone and `r hdci("sites_searched", score = "random")` under random selection. The combined ranking avoided `r hdci("low_avoided")` of low-density dives and `r hdci("ghost_avoided")` of ghost dives at this retention. These are retained outcomes from observed dives; they do not establish the number of aggregations missed or the consequences of deferring unvisited sites.

The acceptable loss makes a large difference. Retaining 99% of >0.04 dives required `r hdci("sites_searched", 0.99)` of site-years with the combined ranking, leaving much less scope to avoid low-density and ghost dives. At the nominal top-85% rank cutoff, the forward ranking searched `r p1(pick(hdfixed, design = "forward", period = "2019-2026", score = "combined", nominal_fraction = 0.85, metric = "sites_searched", col = "value"))` of candidate site-years and missed `r cip(pick(hdfixed, design = "forward", period = "2019-2026", score = "combined", nominal_fraction = 0.85, metric = "high_missed", col = "value"), pick(hdfixed, design = "forward", period = "2019-2026", score = "combined", nominal_fraction = 0.85, metric = "high_missed", col = "low"), pick(hdfixed, design = "forward", period = "2019-2026", score = "combined", nominal_fraction = 0.85, metric = "high_missed", col = "high"), 1)` of >0.04 dives. The proposed 10–15% search reduction therefore cannot be assumed compatible with negligible omissions; the allowed omission rate must be agreed and tested in the field.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-high-density
#| tbl-cap: "Unchanged rankings evaluated at >0.04 CPUE. Percentage of designated cull site-years selected for dives and low-density or ghost dives avoided at matched high-density retention; brackets are 95% paired reef-year bootstrap intervals. Low-density means positive CPUE <0.02. Spatial: 2018–2026; forward evidence test: 2019–2026."
hdrows <- expand.grid(design = c("spatial", "forward"), target = c(0.8, 0.9, 0.95, 0.99), score = c("habitat", "combined"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
hval <- function(metric, i) {
  x <- hdrows[i, ]; period <- if (x$design == "spatial") "2018-2026" else "2019-2026"
  sprintf("%.1f [%.1f–%.1f]", 100 * hd(metric, x$target, x$score, x$design, period),
          100 * hd(metric, x$target, x$score, x$design, period, "low"),
          100 * hd(metric, x$target, x$score, x$design, period, "high"))
}
hdrows <- hdrows[order(hdrows$design, hdrows$target, hdrows$score), ]
knitr::kable(data.frame(Test = hdrows$design, `Retention (%)` = 100 * hdrows$target,
  Ranking = ifelse(hdrows$score == "combined", "Habitat + evidence", "Habitat"),
  `Cull sites selected (%)` = vapply(seq_len(nrow(hdrows)), function(i) hval("sites_searched", i), character(1)),
  `Low avoided (%)` = vapply(seq_len(nrow(hdrows)), function(i) hval("low_avoided", i), character(1)),
  `Ghost avoided (%)` = vapply(seq_len(nrow(hdrows)), function(i) hval("ghost_avoided", i), character(1)), check.names = FALSE))
```

The full retention curve is shown above (@fig-high-density); the compact A–C comparison is in the main Results (@tbl-operational-highlights).

Intermediate dives were tracked separately rather than treated as failed high-density detections. At 95% >0.04 retention, the forward combined ranking retained `r hdci("intermediate_retained")` of dives from 0.02 to 0.04 inclusive. Allowing their omission in the management criterion did not itself change the search order: the saved model still learned the original ≥0.02 response and recent crew observations. The spatial comparison and manta-habitat alternatives were likewise rescored without refitting. Full fixed-effort, matched-retention, paired-difference and per-season results are provided in `cull_high_density_*.csv`.

### Manta effort paired with the site-selection decisions {.unnumbered}

The spatial effort estimate used `r int(opcover$manta_valid_segments)` valid tow segments from `r int(opcover$manta_reef_years)` of the `r int(opcover$reef_years)` evaluated reef-years, totalling `r num(opcover$manta_straight_distance_km, 0)` km of straight-line distance. Of `r int(opcover$manta_records)` tow records on these reef-years, `r int(opcover$manta_excluded)` lacked usable segment geometry or had zero length and were excluded from both tow denominators. Designated sites contained `r p1(opcover$distance_inside_sites)` of the valid distance; `r p1(opcover$tows_entirely_inside_sites)` of whole segments lay entirely inside designated sites. Surveillance outside that footprint remains in the calculation at every cutoff.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-manta-effort-full
#| tbl-cap: "Spatial manta-effort proxies at matched >0.04 dive retention, all three rankings. Percentages [95% reef-year bootstrap intervals]. These conditional estimates retain surveillance outside designated sites and do not measure detection after tow removal."
full_manta <- expand.grid(target = c(.8,.9,.95,.99), score = c("combined","habitat","random"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
full_manta <- full_manta[order(full_manta$target, full_manta$score), ]
mval <- function(metric) vapply(seq_len(nrow(full_manta)), function(i) {
  t <- full_manta$target[i]; s <- full_manta$score[i]
  sprintf("%.1f [%.1f–%.1f]", 100 * om(metric,t,s), 100 * om(metric,t,s,"low"), 100 * om(metric,t,s,"high"))
}, "")
knitr::kable(data.frame(`Dive retention (%)` = 100 * full_manta$target,
  Ranking = c(combined="Habitat + recent observations",habitat="Habitat alone",random="Random selection")[full_manta$score],
  `Whole tows avoided (%)` = mval("manta_tows_avoided"),
  `Tow distance avoided (%)` = mval("manta_distance_avoided"), check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE)
```

The class A–C cutoff in the main Results uses the product's descending-rank/site-count rule. The older `cull_high_density_priority_classes.csv` instead uses a percentile threshold and is retained as an archived analytical comparison. It should not be substituted for the exact product cutoff, particularly on reefs with few sites. The matching values for the current operational rule are in `operational_priority_cutoff.csv`; `operational_tow_effort_matched.csv` and `operational_tow_effort_fixed.csv` retain the full spatial effort comparisons.

### Each source covers the other's gaps {.unnumbered}

#### Habitat layers: a consistent first ordering on every reef {.unnumbered}

The habitat layers cover every reef. They give a consistent ordering within each reef, which is useful wherever crews have little recent evidence. Across the GBR, each layer's absolute values mostly reflect survey year and region (@fig-overview). Within reefs, the cull-trained layers placed their highest ranks along reef margins and outer slopes (@fig-maps).

![The three main habitat layers across the Great Barrier Reef, shown as cell means at about 2.9 km. The two cull-trained layers (left, centre) are annual probabilities of a problematic cull site-year in 2026; the HMSC layer (right) is conditional on an active reef-year. Gaps in RG + year are reefs without ReefGuide layers, filled by the clean + year fallback in the primary search-planning layer.](../outputs/figures/fig01_gbr_overview.png){#fig-overview width="100%"}

See @fig-maps in the main habitat Results. Imagery attribution: Tiles © Esri — Source: Esri, i-cubed, USDA, USGS, AEX, GeoEye, Getmapping, Aerogrid, IGN, IGP, UPR-EGP, and the GIS User Community.

On their own, the layers discriminate modestly between places on the same reef. On independent manta tows, RG + year reached a within reef-year AUC of `r ci3(mi("RG + year", "within_reef_year_auc"), mi("RG + year", "auc_low"), mi("RG + year", "auc_high"))` (@tbl-manta, @fig-manta). It placed `r p0(mi("RG + year", "top20_lift") - 1)` more strong-evidence tows in each reef's top-ranked 20% than chance. The manta model, trained on tows but scored leave-reef-out, reached `r ci3(mt("within", "auc"), mt("within", "auc", "low"), mt("within", "auc", "high"))` (Appendix H).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-manta
#| tbl-cap: "Discrimination between strong-evidence and strictly negative manta tows within reef-years. Manta tows were not used to fit any of these layers. Lift is the share of strong-evidence tows in a reef-year's top 20% of tows, divided by 20%. Intervals are 95% bootstrap intervals over reef-years."
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Layer = mic$layer,
  `Within reef-year AUC (95% CI)` = sprintf("%s (%s–%s)", a3(mic$within_reef_year_auc), a3(mic$auc_low), a3(mic$auc_high)),
  `Top-20% lift (95% CI)` = sprintf("%s (%s–%s)", a2(mic$top20_lift), a2(mic$lift_low), a2(mic$lift_high)),
  check.names = FALSE), align = "lll")
```

![Independent manta tow check of the three habitat layers. Left: within reef-year AUC; right: top-20% lift. Bars are 95% bootstrap intervals over reef-years; dotted lines mark chance.](../outputs/figures/fig03_manta_independent_check.png){#fig-manta width="100%"}

The layers agree only in part on which cells rank highest. Median within-reef Spearman correlations were `r a2(pick(la, pair = "Clean + year vs RG + year", col = "median"))` between clean + year and RG + year, `r a2(pick(la, pair = "Clean + year vs HMSC joint", col = "median"))` between clean + year and HMSC, and `r a2(pick(la, pair = "RG + year vs HMSC joint", col = "median"))` between RG + year and HMSC (Appendix D). Where both cull-trained layers exist, the fallback and RG rankings correlate at `r a2(fbc$spearman)`, so ranks near the RG coverage boundary within a reef are less reliable.

#### Habitat alone as a cull-site ranking {.unnumbered}

Used alone to rank all designated sites on a reef, the held-out habitat layer retained problematic dives only slightly faster than low-density or ghost dives (@tbl-sites, @fig-sites). Searching the top 70% of sites retained `r cip(cs("problematic_dives_kept", 0.7), cs("problematic_dives_kept", 0.7, col = "low"), cs("problematic_dives_kept", 0.7, col = "high"))` of problematic dives. A ranking with no information would have retained `r p1(cs("dives_kept", 0.7))`, the share of all dives at those sites. Within reef-years, the AUC was `r a2(pick(csa, period = "2018-2026", score = "leave-reef-out", col = "auc_problematic_vs_low"))` for problematic versus low-density dives and `r a2(pick(csa, period = "2018-2026", score = "leave-reef-out", col = "auc_problematic_vs_ghost"))` versus ghost dives. The in-sample layer looked stronger (`r a2(pick(csa, period = "2018-2026", score = "deployed", col = "auc_problematic_vs_low"))` and `r a2(pick(csa, period = "2018-2026", score = "deployed", col = "auc_problematic_vs_ghost"))`) only because it had been trained on those dives.

Whether a site holding COTS is above or below the action threshold on a given visit depends mainly on irruption stage, earlier culling and the movement of aggregations. Recent evidence captures these; static habitat cannot. The habitat ranking does reach places crews have not tested: `r p0(pick(und, top30 = TRUE, col = "share_never_dived"))` of site-years ranked in a reef's top 30% were at sites that had never been dived.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sites
#| tbl-cap: "Diving only the top-ranked designated cull sites on each reef, held-out habitat ranking alone, 2018–2026. 'Dives kept' is what a ranking with no information would retain of every outcome. Brackets: 95% bootstrap interval over reef-years."
s <- c(0.8, 0.7, 0.6, 0.5)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  `Cull sites selected for dives` = paste("top", p0(s)),
  `Dives kept (no-information baseline)` = vapply(s, function(x) p1(cs("dives_kept", x)), ""),
  `Problematic dives kept` = vapply(s, function(x) sprintf("%s (%s–%s)", p1(cs("problematic_dives_kept", x)), p1(cs("problematic_dives_kept", x, col = "low")), p1(cs("problematic_dives_kept", x, col = "high"))), ""),
  `Low-density dives avoided` = vapply(s, function(x) p1(cs("low_dives_avoided", x)), ""),
  `Ghost dives avoided` = vapply(s, function(x) p1(cs("ghost_dives_avoided", x)), ""),
  check.names = FALSE), align = "lllll")
```

![Original ≥0.02 evaluation: share of cull dives that would still occur if only the highest-ranked designated cull sites on each reef were dived, ranked by habitat alone, by dive outcome. Left: held-out ranking; right: deployed layer (in-sample). The dashed diagonal is the share of sites dived. Bands are 95% bootstrap intervals over reef-years. Without recent evidence, problematic, low-density and ghost dives fall away at almost the same rate.](../outputs/figures/fig14_cull_search_area.png){#fig-sites width="100%"}

#### Cull history: strong where it exists {.unnumbered}

Problematic sites persist between seasons at a scale of about 0.5–1 km. In the strictly forward test, the blend of habitat and cull history reached a within reef-year AUC of `r ci3(fvh("combined_fixed"), fvh("combined_fixed", col = "auc_low"), fvh("combined_fixed", col = "auc_high"))`, against `r a3(fvh("habitat"))` for habitat alone (@tbl-forward, @fig-forward).

The forecast is strongest where history exists. It reached `r a3(fvh("combined_fixed", "with nearby history"))` with history nearby, `r a3(fvh("combined_fixed", "little or no nearby history"))` where history was sparse and `r a3(fvh("combined_fixed", "new sites"))` at sites never culled before. History lies within reach of only `r p1(hist$fraction_with_history)` of 120 m reef cells, so across most of the reef the blend falls back to habitat.

Part of the skill reflects operator behaviour: a score based only on how often crews had dived a site reached `r a3(fvh("effort"))`. This layer is therefore delivered as a map of **known aggregation sites** for briefing crews, not as habitat. Reef-context predictors at 0.5–1 km (windward position, distance to reef edge, channels, eReefs currents) did not improve habitat forecasts robustly (`r a3(fvh("habitat_context"))` vs `r a3(fvh("habitat"))`, overlapping intervals).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-forward
#| tbl-cap: "Forward validation: within reef-year AUC for problematic cull site-years, test years 2022–2026 pooled. Each score uses only data from before the test year. The deployed blend's 95% bootstrap interval over reef-years is given for all site-years."
meth <- c(habitat = "Habitat (HMSC refitted before test year)", habitat_context = "Habitat + reef context",
          effort = "Dive effort only", history_fixed = "History kernel", combined_fixed = "Habitat + history (deployed)")
subs <- c("all", "with nearby history", "little or no nearby history", "new sites")
tf <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(meth), function(m) {
  v <- vapply(subs, function(s) a3(fvh(m, s)), "")
  v[1] <- if (m == "combined_fixed") ci3(fvh(m), fvh(m, col = "auc_low"), fvh(m, col = "auc_high")) else v[1]
  data.frame(Score = meth[[m]], t(v), check.names = FALSE)
}))
names(tf)[-1] <- sprintf("%s (n = %s)", c("All site-years", "With nearby history", "Little or none", "New sites"),
                         vapply(subs, function(s) int(fvh("habitat", s, col = "site_years")), ""))
knitr::kable(tf, row.names = FALSE, align = "lllll")
```

![Forward validation of habitat, reef context and cull-history scores. Left: all test site-years with 95% bootstrap intervals over reef-years. Right: the same scores split by how much cull history lies within reach of the site. History carries the forecast where it exists; habitat carries it where history is absent.](../outputs/figures/fig09_forward_validation.png){#fig-forward width="100%"}

#### Where recent evidence is missing {.unnumbered}

Recent evidence is unevenly spread. `r p0(1 - pick(ecov, window = "last_season", col = "share_reef_any_prev"))` of reef-years were on reefs not visited the season before. On those reefs (`r int(nv_dives)` dives) every ranking was close to chance (AUC about `r a2(pick(eauc, window = "last_season", subset = "reef not visited", score = "combined", col = "auc_problematic_vs_low"))`), and habitat was the only information available.

Habitat also reaches ground that recent search has not covered. A tow was counted as *new ground* if no tow lay within 300 m in the previous five seasons. On new ground, the manta model ranked tows with a within reef-year AUC of `r ci3(pick(eng, ground = "new ground", score = "manta_within", metric = "auc", col = "value"), pick(eng, ground = "new ground", score = "manta_within", metric = "auc", col = "low"), pick(eng, ground = "new ground", score = "manta_within", metric = "auc", col = "high"))`, and the cull-trained layer at `r a2(pick(eng, ground = "new ground", score = "cull", metric = "auc", col = "value"))`. Strong evidence was more common on new ground than on repeat ground (`r p1(pick(eng, ground = "new ground", score = "cull", metric = "auc", col = "strong_share"))` vs `r p1(pick(eng, ground = "repeat ground", score = "cull", metric = "auc", col = "strong_share"))` of tows), partly because new ground is often surveyed early in an irruption. This is the basis for the exploration areas in the 2027 product.

### Manta surveillance: spread tows evenly, add where habitat ranks highest {.unnumbered}

**Systematic thinning found the most aggregations at every level of effort** (@tbl-thinning, @fig-aggregations-detail). With 60% of tows kept, it found `r p1(ag(0.6, "systematic"))` of the `r int(ag(0.6, "aggregations"))` aggregations of two or more strong-evidence tows in `r int(ag(0.6, "surveys"))` surveys. Random thinning found `r p1(ag(0.6, "random"))`, and thinning by the held-out cull-trained layer found `r cip(ag(0.6, "layer_cv"), ag(0.6, "layer_cv_low"), ag(0.6, "layer_cv_high"))`.

The largest cut that still found at least 95% of aggregations was:

- `r p0(mx("systematic_point"))` of tows for systematic thinning (`r p0(mx("systematic_assured"))` with bootstrap assurance);
- `r p0(mx("random_point"))` for random thinning;
- `r p0(mx("layer_cv_point"))` for thinning by habitat rank.

Results for 2022–2026 alone were the same: `r p0(mx("systematic_point", AGG_RECENT))`, `r p0(mx("random_point", AGG_RECENT))` and `r p0(mx("layer_cv_point", AGG_RECENT))`.

Ranking concentrates the kept tows in a few high-scoring stretches of reef, so aggregations in low-scoring stretches are missed entirely. Habitat rank is therefore not a good basis for dropping tows. It did find slightly more isolated single strong tows than random (`r p0(ag(0.6, "layer_cv", "isolated strong tows, all years"))` vs `r p0(ag(0.6, "random", "isolated strong tows, all years"))` at 60% kept). Scoring with the deployed (in-sample) layer instead of the held-out one overstated aggregations found by `r pp(ag(0.6, "layer_deployed") - ag(0.6, "layer_cv"))` percentage points at 60% kept.

Reef-level detection is robust to thinning whichever tows are kept. Irruption reef-years have many positive tows, so keeping about 60% of tows in 2022–2026 still flagged `r p0(op("Manta: outbreak reef-years still detected", "primary_layer"))` of irruption reef-years with the layer and `r p0(op("Manta: outbreak reef-years still detected", "random"))` at random (Appendix D).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-thinning
#| tbl-cap: "Share of COTS aggregations (two or more strong-evidence tows within 500 m) still found when manta tows are cut within each survey, all years. The layer is the cull-trained RG + year model scored leave-reef-out; the deployed column is the same layer scored in-sample. Brackets: 95% bootstrap interval over surveys."
k <- c(0.8, 0.7, 0.6, 0.5)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  `Tows kept` = p0(k),
  `Layer, held out` = sprintf("%s (%s–%s)", vapply(k, function(x) p1(ag(x, "layer_cv")), ""),
                              vapply(k, function(x) p1(ag(x, "layer_cv_low")), ""), vapply(k, function(x) p1(ag(x, "layer_cv_high")), "")),
  `Layer, deployed` = vapply(k, function(x) p1(ag(x, "layer_deployed")), ""),
  Random = vapply(k, function(x) p1(ag(x, "random")), ""),
  Systematic = vapply(k, function(x) p1(ag(x, "systematic")), ""),
  check.names = FALSE), align = "lllll")
```

![Manta tows kept versus COTS aggregations found. Left: aggregations of two or more strong-evidence tows found as tows are cut, for the cull-trained layer (held out and deployed), random selection and systematic thinning; bands are 95% bootstrap intervals over surveys. Right: share found at 60% of tows kept, by aggregation size. Evenly spaced thinning loses the fewest aggregations.](../outputs/figures/fig13_manta_aggregation_cv.png){#fig-aggregations-detail width="100%"}

**A habitat model trained on manta tows is the best guide to where to add tows.** Manta tows provide about 20 times more training rows than cull site-years. The within reef-year manta model ranked held-out tows best (@tbl-mantamodel, @fig-manta-model). It found `r pp(pick(mra, strategy = "within_cv", keep = 0.6, col = "within_minus_cull"))` percentage points more aggregations than the cull-trained model at 60% kept (95% CI `r gpp(pick(mra, strategy = "within_cv", keep = 0.6, col = "within_minus_cull_low"), pick(mra, strategy = "within_cv", keep = 0.6, col = "within_minus_cull_high"))`). That is still below random (`r p1(pick(mra, strategy = "random", keep = 0.6, col = "found"))`) and systematic thinning (`r p1(pick(mra, strategy = "systematic", keep = 0.6, col = "found"))`), so its role is to direct extra tows rather than to remove them. Its top predictors were wave period and height, bathymetry and slope.

Training on manta did not improve cull-site selection. With survey year as a predictor, the manta model ranked cull dives at chance (AUC `r a2(pick(mrc, period = "2018-2026", score = "manta", col = "auc_problematic_vs_low"))`), because survey year took `r p0(year_gain_manta)` of its fitted gain. The within reef-year version matched the cull-trained model over 2018–2026 (`r a3(pick(mrc, period = "2018-2026", score = "within", col = "auc_problematic_vs_low"))` vs `r a3(pick(mrc, period = "2018-2026", score = "cull", col = "auc_problematic_vs_low"))`). Once last season's evidence was added, every habitat model gave the same result. Manta tows see COTS and scars from the surface along the reef perimeter, whereas a problematic dive measures how many COTS a diver finds in a site; the two are related but not the same.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-mantamodel
#| tbl-cap: "Cull-trained and manta-trained habitat models on held-out manta tows (all three fitted on the same leave-reef-out folds). AUC: strong-evidence vs strictly negative tows within reef-years, with 95% bootstrap intervals. Aggregations: share found at 60% of tows kept."
mods <- c(cull = "Cull-trained", manta = "Manta-trained (with year)", within = "Manta-trained, within reef-year")
strat <- c(cull = "cull_cv", manta = "manta_cv", within = "within_cv")
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Model = unname(mods),
  `Tow AUC (95% CI)` = vapply(names(mods), function(m) sprintf("%s (%s–%s)", a3(mt(m, "auc")), a3(mt(m, "auc", "low")), a3(mt(m, "auc", "high"))), ""),
  `Top-20% lift` = vapply(names(mods), function(m) a2(mt(m, "lift")), ""),
  `Aggregations found, 60% kept` = vapply(names(mods), function(m) p1(pick(mra, strategy = strat[[m]], keep = 0.6, col = "found")), ""),
  check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE, align = "llll")
```

![Cull-trained and manta-trained habitat models on both goals. Left: within reef-year AUC on held-out manta tows. Centre: aggregations found with 60% of tows kept, with random and systematic thinning for reference. Right: low-density cull dives avoided at 90% of problematic dives (CPUE ≥0.02) retained, for the habitat model alone and with last season's evidence. Bars are 95% bootstrap intervals. The manta model ranks tows best; for cull sites, last season's evidence brings every habitat model to the same result.](../outputs/figures/fig16_manta_response_model.png){#fig-manta-model width="100%"}

### The 2027 cull-site priority ranking and exploration areas {.unnumbered}

Every designated cull site (`r int(n_sites)` sites on `r int(n_reefs)` reefs) was ranked within its reef for the 2027 season, using the combined model with the most recent 12 months of evidence. The ranking is delivered as a CSV and as the EoTR cull-site KMZ, with each polygon coloured by priority class. Each polygon also carries its rank, its modelled chance of a problematic dive if dived, and last season's evidence. @tbl-classes shows what each class kept in the forward test.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-classes
#| tbl-cap: "Original ≥0.02 evaluation: 2027 priority classes and what searching through each class retained in the forward test (dives 2019–2026)."
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  `Searching through` = c("A", "A + B", "A + B + C", "All (incl. D)"),
  `Sites on the reef` = c("top 20%", "top 50%", "top 80%", "100%"),
  `Problematic dives kept` = p0(cls$problematic_dives_kept),
  `Low-density dives avoided` = p0(cls$low_dives_avoided),
  `Ghost dives avoided` = p0(cls$ghost_dives_avoided),
  check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE, align = "lllll")
```

The archived percentile-cutoff summary (@tbl-high-density-classes) retains the earlier analytical definition. Its nominal top-80% cutoff retained `r p1(pick(hdclasses, nominal_fraction = 0.8, metric = "high_retained", col = "value"))` of observed >0.04 dives. It differs slightly from the product's exact A–C rule, which retained `r p1(oc("high_retained"))`, because the two definitions round site counts differently on small reefs. Use @tbl-search-highlights for the operational A–C trade-off. Neither cutoff is an established safe stopping point.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-high-density-classes
#| tbl-cap: "Archived percentile-rank cutoffs, forward test of 2019–2026. These are not the product's integer priority-class cutoffs. Retained shares are percentages [95% reef-year bootstrap intervals]. Intermediate means 0.02–0.04 inclusive; high-density means >0.04. No annual effort saving is inferred."
class_fractions <- c(0.2, 0.5, 0.8, 1)
class_cell <- function(a, metric) {
  x <- hdclasses[hdclasses$nominal_fraction == a & hdclasses$metric == metric, ]
  stopifnot(nrow(x) == 1)
  sprintf("%.1f [%.1f–%.1f]", 100 * x$value, 100 * x$low, 100 * x$high)
}
knitr::kable(data.frame(`Percentile selection` = c("Top 20%", "Top 50%", "Top 80%", "All"),
  `Rank cutoff (%)` = 100 * class_fractions,
  `High-density retained (%)` = vapply(class_fractions, class_cell, character(1), metric = "high_retained"),
  `Intermediate retained (%)` = vapply(class_fractions, class_cell, character(1), metric = "intermediate_retained"),
  check.names = FALSE))
```

The two sources share the ranking:

- **Evidence ranks the top.** `r int(n_probev)` sites had a problematic dive last season and `r int(n_mantaev)` have strong manta evidence nearby.
- **Evidence also lowers sites.** `r int(n_quiet)` sites were dived last season with nothing problematic, which strongly lowers their rank.
- **Habitat ranks the rest.** `r int(n_noev)` sites (`r p0(n_noev / nrow(pri))`) are on reefs with no dives or tows in the last 12 months. Habitat alone orders them, as a first search order to update once manta tows come in.

The exploration layer adds high-ranked habitat outside the current search footprint (@fig-2027), so that the ranking does not keep consolidating search on the same places. It contains `r int(nrow(expl))` areas on `r int(length(unique(expl$reef_name)))` reefs, with a median size of `r num(median(expl$area_ha), 0)` ha, a median habitat percentile of `r a2(median(expl$habitat_percentile))`, and a median distance from a cull site of `r int(median(expl$nearest_cull_site_m))` m. On well-surveyed reefs such as Batt and Eyrie, cull sites and five seasons of tows already cover most high-ranked habitat. The larger opportunities are on reefs with little recent towing.

See the seasonal-product example in Methods (@fig-2027).

## Appendix I: Updated metacommunity calibration and exploratory projections {.unnumbered}

This appendix reports the completed 21 October 2026 figure set for the current working model, identified in the source files as W-wave-lf04. The COTS and coral comparison combines source Figures 1 and 4 in @fig-metacommunity-cots-coral. The remaining figures appear below, with panels rearranged for portrait pages and the source summaries and uncertainty bands retained. Appendix J preserves the 15 October snapshot as a development record.

### Calibration updates and uncertainty {.unnumbered}

Since the earlier snapshot, the working model has incorporated revised coral thermal responses, a chlorophyll-based larval-survival modifier, wave-exposure effects on settlement, and revised initial population and coral settings. Initial fast-growing coral at Lizard Island was increased by 0.04 in absolute cover. Larger increases were rejected because they left too many COTS between irruptions. The linear observation conversion remains 0.015 COTS per tow per adult per hectare; nonlinear alternatives failed regional checks. These decisions improved the working calibration without identifying a unique population mechanism [@adriacalibrationreport2026].

The comparison comprises `r int(mcn("base_seeds"))` base seed pairs plus twelve one-at-a-time parameter perturbations of ±25%, giving `r int(mcn("calibration_arms_per_cull_state"))` runs in each culling state. Perturbations cover outside larval supply, background coral mortality, bleaching under low heat stress, the chlorophyll response, juvenile survival and initial fast-growing coral shares. Inner bands span the base seeds; outer bands span all runs. Neither is a probability interval, and joint parameter and structural uncertainty are not fully represented.

Recorded cull totals are now distributed among sites on the same reef in proportion to simulated population counts, retaining juvenile/adult stages and pre-/post-spawning timing. Removals remain limited by the animals available. This replaces the spatial-kernel allocation in the earlier diagnostic. Calibration scoring keeps culling off; paired culling-on runs provide the overlay. Earlier unmet-removal percentages therefore do not describe the current model.

### Recent densities and additional reefs {.unnumbered}

The recent-density comparison (@fig-metacommunity-recent-density) shows partial agreement with diver estimates and differences among reefs. Corrected external irruption probabilities and density targets share cull and SALAD evidence, so this is a diagnostic comparison. The additional reefs (@fig-metacommunity-additional) show the contrast between historical irruption reefs and low-density ribbon reefs, while individual peak timing and size remain imperfect. These checks do not complete regional validation; Ribbon No 10 has no LTMP series here.
